Competition day from start to finish

The day starts at registration: the shooter confirms the entry, receives a competitor number and pins it on the upper back, fully visible. Then everyone checks the squad lists and the shooting times. A squad is a group of up to six shooters, drawn by lot, who shoot together. Keeping to the timetable is the shooter’s own responsibility.

Arrive early: registration, finding your squad and getting ready all take time. The number goes between the shoulders and the waist, not folded or cut. Put on hearing protection and safety glasses before you go to the stand. In both disciplines a shooter who turns up without them counts as absent, and the rules for late shooters apply (see below).

Dress neatly and safely: shorts may end no more than 5 cm above the knee, tops need sleeves and sandals are not allowed. Carry your gun open (broken at the hinge, so everyone can see it is not loaded) and without a sling. A semi-automatic is carried with its breech open (the bolt held back). All the rules: Dress code and safety on the stand.

Want to check that your gun works? Do it before the round, at a special test stand if the ground has one. Test shots on a competition stand are not allowed.

Parcours de Chasse – Sporting™

Nobody may practise on the competition layouts before the event. Practise on other ranges.

Compak® Sporting

You may practise on the same target flights (trajectories) as in the competition, but the trajectory setting table must be a different one. This table is the scheme that says which traps are shot from each station. At continental and world championships official practice opens on the Saturday before the championship.

In Parcours de Chasse – Sporting™ the squad shoots all the singles of a stand first, then the doubles, and at each new stand a different shooter goes first. Before anyone shoots, the first shooter of the squad is shown the targets: each one is thrown so that its flight can be seen.

Compak® Sporting

When Compak® Sporting is shot by squad, a full squad has six shooters: five stand on the five stations and the sixth waits behind station 1. With fewer shooters one station stays empty. When everyone has shot their targets from their station, the squad moves one station to the right. The shooter from station 5 goes to wait behind station 1, and the waiting shooter steps onto station 1. This goes on until each shooter has shot from all five stations. Before your round, go to the Compak field you have been assigned to and report to the referee: this is compulsory. In Compak in line shooters do not move as a squad: they enter station 1 one by one and walk along the line to station 5.

Where this is in the rules: Chapter 17 · Squad rotation through the stations

Tip: When your turn comes, be ready at once, with cartridges for the whole round. In Compak® Sporting the referee does not have to look for a missing shooter. How the stands work: How a Sporting™ layout and round work and How a Compak® Sporting layout works.

A round is 25 targets: one layout in Sporting™, one field in Compak® Sporting. An international competition is 200 targets, so eight rounds over several days. The referee marks each target on the score sheet, usually X for a hit and O for a miss. In Sporting™ shooters check their score when leaving a stand; in Compak® Sporting they sign the sheet at the end of the round.

Being late is costly. In Sporting™ the referee calls the shooter’s name three times within one minute; a shooter who misses their turn gets zeros for the targets not shot. In Compak® Sporting a shooter who turns up once the first shooter of the squad has already called for the first target (asked for it to be thrown) gets 25 zeros for the round.

Compak® Sporting

In Compak in line you count as late when two things have happened: the computer system has cancelled your competitor number, and the next shooter is on station 1. The penalty is the same: 25 zeros for the round.

Where this is in the rules: Chapter 9 · Late in Compak in line: 25 zeros

Tip: Late for a reason outside your control? Do not rejoin the squad on your own: appeal in writing to the jury (the panel in charge of the competition), in Compak® Sporting on the same day. If the jury agrees, you shoot the round with another squad. Details: The call, time limits and lateness.

If shooters tie for one of the top three places, the tie is settled by a shoot-off of 25 targets, then sudden death if the scores are still level. In sudden death they keep shooting, and the first one to miss is out. Below third place there is no shoot-off: tied shooters share the place. Countback sets their order in the list: their scores are compared on the 8th layout or Compak first, then on the 7th, and so on back to the 1st. The day ends with the results board and the prize-giving.

Tip: Might you be in a shoot-off? Stay close and reachable: you may have to shoot within 15 minutes of the call. At international events all prize winners must attend the prize giving, in team outfit or smart trousers and a blazer. How to read the results: How to read a scoreboard and results.

Key points

  • Registration, competitor number on the back, squad lists and times.
  • Without hearing protection and safety glasses on the stand you are treated as absent.
  • Be ready at your turn, with cartridges for the whole round; test the gun only at the test stand.
  • Lateness costs zeros; in Compak® Sporting 25 zeros for the round.
  • Top-three ties: shoot-off of 25, then sudden death; lower ties: countback.

Did you know?

In Sporting™ the squad waits as close to the stand as possible, but in a place where it does not distract the person shooting.

Stand Talk

  • Coach You’re in squad twelve, starting on layout five at nine-thirty.

    Meaning: Squad number, start layout and start time.

  • Coach Check your card before you leave the stand.

    Meaning: Sporting™: make sure the referee recorded your score correctly now; later it is too late.

  • Coach Twenty-two in the first round is fine — seven more to go.

    Meaning: 22 out of 25 in the first round; seven rounds remain in a 200-target event.

  • Coach Stay close — if it’s a tie, you shoot within fifteen minutes of the call.

    Meaning: A shooter who may be in a shoot-off must be ready soon after being called.

For the interpreter
  • ClayAway tours, which are being prepared, will also use “squad” for a subgroup of a tour. At a competition it means the shooting group, so make clear which one you mean.
For parents
  • Watch from the spectators’ area and stay quiet near the stand. Advice called out during the round counts as coaching: the referee can give your child a yellow card for it. More: Juniors and parents: support without pressure.

Check yourself · 3 questions

  1. What happens if you come to the stand without hearing protection or safety glasses?

    1. You may shoot, but you get a warning
    2. You are treated as absent and may not shoot
    3. The referee gives you a spare set
    Answer

    You are treated as absent and may not shoot

    In both disciplines a shooter without hearing protection or safety glasses is treated as absent, and the lateness rules apply.

    Chapter 8 · Hearing protection is compulsory

  2. Where may you check that your gun works?

    1. On the first competition stand, before the round
    2. Anywhere on the ground, if the area is clear
    3. At a special test stand, if the ground has one
    Answer

    At a special test stand, if the ground has one

    Test shots on a competition stand are not allowed in either discipline; use the test stand.

    Chapter 3 · No test shots on the stand

  3. In Compak® Sporting shot by squad, a shooter arrives after the first shooter has called for the first target. What happens?

    1. Nothing, he joins in
    2. He gets 25 zeros for that round
    3. He shoots the round alone later without penalty
    4. He loses one target
    Answer

    He gets 25 zeros for that round

    In Compak® Sporting shot by squad, arriving after the first call costs 25 zeros for the round. For a reason outside your control, you can appeal to the jury in writing on the same day.

    Chapter 9 · Late in squad shooting: 25 zeros
